background_notes.fact: For the normalized Fourier Sobolev norms, r<=s implies ||h||_(H^r)<=||h||_(H^s), and ||partial_x h||_(H^s)<=||h||_(H^(s+1)) for smooth h. S_t is an isometry commuting with partial_x,Dinv and P. P and Dinv are contractions on L^2, and Dinv partial_x h=P h. Consequently Dinv B_t(u,v)=S_(-t)P[(S_t u)(S_t v)] for smooth u,v; B has zero mean.

background_notes.justification: These follow coefficientwise: (1+k^2)^r<=(1+k^2)^s, k^2<=(1+k^2), |1/k|<=1 for nonzero integer k, and (ik)^(-1)(ik)=1 off zero. These facts justify the norm inclusions in S001, derivative estimate in S002, and contractions and product identity in S003.

background_notes.justification: Rapid decay of smooth Fourier coefficients permits termwise spatial and time differentiation of the multiplier expressions, uniformly on compact time intervals. Products preserve smoothness. In Rem, the convolution of rapidly decreasing coefficients stays rapidly decreasing even after multiplication by any fixed power of the output frequency, since |eta|<=2 and |k|^(-1)<=1 off zero; thus W is spatially smooth. For continuous G, the difference quotient of its primitive is the average of G over a shrinking interval, which tends in norm to G(t) by continuity. The integral norm bound follows from triangle inequalities on Riemann sums, and bounded linear maps pass through their norm limits. Applying these facts to D022 gives all derivatives and initial values used in S001-S004, without any approximation of rough data. Zero-length integrals at t=a vanish, so the Ctri estimates there require no convention for 0^0.
